stem: A printer prints 4 pages per second. At this rate, how many pages does it print in 3 minutes?
explanation: Convert the time with a factor that cancels minutes: $3\text{ min}\cdot\frac{60\text{ s}}{1\text{ min}}=180\text{ s}$. Then $180\cdot4=720$ pages.

choiceExplanations.A: Multiplies 4 by 3 without converting minutes to seconds.
choiceExplanations.B: Divides 180 seconds by 4; a rate in pages per second is multiplied by the seconds.
choiceExplanations.C: This is the number of pages printed in one minute, not three.
choiceExplanations.E: Uses 3,600 seconds per minute; 3,600 is the number of seconds in an hour.

stem: Compare Quantity A and Quantity B, using additional information centered above the two quantities if such information is given.
explanation: Chain the factors: $1\text{ wk}\cdot\frac{7\text{ d}}{1\text{ wk}}\cdot\frac{24\text{ h}}{1\text{ d}}\cdot\frac{60\text{ min}}{1\text{ h}}=10{,}080$ minutes, which is greater than 10,000.

content.quantityA: The number of minutes in 1 week

stem: A train travels at a constant speed of 90 kilometers per hour. What is its speed, in meters per second?
explanation: Convert the top and bottom units separately: $90\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}}\cdot\frac{1000\text{ m}}{1\text{ km}}\cdot\frac{1\text{ h}}{3600\text{ s}}=\frac{90{,}000}{3600}=25$ meters per second.

choiceExplanations.A: Divides 90 by 60: that is kilometers per minute, and the kilometers were never converted.
choiceExplanations.C: Multiplies by 3.6 instead of dividing: the hour factor was put the wrong way up.
choiceExplanations.D: This is meters per minute; minutes still have to be converted to seconds.
choiceExplanations.E: This is meters per hour; the hours were never converted.

stem: If gasoline costs \$3.80 per gallon, what is the cost, in dollars, of the gasoline that car Q uses to travel 285 miles?
explanation: Fuel used $=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{efficiency}}=\frac{285}{30}=9.5$ gallons. Cost $=9.5\cdot3.80=36.10$ dollars. The tank capacity is not needed.

figure.title: Four cars: fuel efficiency and tank size

stem: Compare Quantity A and Quantity B, using additional information centered above the two quantities if such information is given.
explanation: Square or cube the length factor. $1\text{ yd}^3=3^3\text{ ft}^3=27\text{ ft}^3$ and $1\text{ ft}^2=12^2\text{ in}^2=144\text{ in}^2$. Quantity B is greater.

content.quantityA: The number of cubic feet in 1 cubic yard
content.quantityB: The number of square inches in 1 square foot

stem: A storage tank in the shape of a rectangular box measures 2 meters by 1.5 meters by 0.8 meter. Given that 1 liter = 1,000 cubic centimeters, what is the capacity of the tank, in liters?
explanation: Volume $=2\cdot1.5\cdot0.8=2.4\text{ m}^3$. Since $1\text{ m}=100\text{ cm}$, $1\text{ m}^3=100^3\text{ cm}^3=1{,}000{,}000\text{ cm}^3$, so the tank holds $2{,}400{,}000\text{ cm}^3$, which is $\frac{2{,}400{,}000}{1000}=2{,}400$ liters.

choiceExplanations.A: Uses the length factor 100 once: $2.4\cdot100=240\text{ cm}^3$, then divides by 1,000.
choiceExplanations.B: This is the volume in cubic meters, not liters.
choiceExplanations.C: Squares the factor ($100^2$) instead of cubing it.
choiceExplanations.E: This is the volume in cubic centimeters; divide by 1,000 to get liters.

stem: A flight leaves city P at 9:40 a.m. local time and lands in city Q at 11:10 a.m. local time on the same day. Local time in city Q is 3 hours behind local time in city P. If the flight covers 2,295 miles, what is its average speed, in miles per hour?
explanation: Put both times on P\'s clock: 11:10 a.m. in Q is 2:10 p.m. in P. The flight lasts from 9:40 a.m. to 2:10 p.m., which is 4.5 hours. Speed $=\frac{2295}{4.5}=510$ miles per hour. (Subtracting the local times directly gives 1.5 hours, a wrong 1,530.)

stem: Water is pumped into an empty cylindrical tank whose circular base has area $16\pi$ square feet and whose height is 9 feet at a constant rate of $12\pi$ cubic feet per minute. How many minutes after the pumping begins will the water be 6 feet deep?
explanation: Volume $=$ base area $\times$ depth, so the depth rises at $\frac{12\pi}{16\pi}=0.75$ foot per minute. Time $=\frac{6}{0.75}=8$ minutes.

choiceExplanations.A: Uses $\pi r=4\pi$ as the base area instead of $\pi r^2=16\pi$.
choiceExplanations.B: Uses the circumference $2\pi r=8\pi$ as if it were the base area.
choiceExplanations.D: This is the time to fill the whole tank (9 feet deep), not to reach 6 feet.
choiceExplanations.E: Uses the diameter 8 in $\pi r^2$, giving a base area of $64\pi$.

stem: Compare Quantity A and Quantity B, using additional information centered above the two quantities if such information is given.
explanation: Fuel used $=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{efficiency}}$, so for a fixed distance it is inversely proportional to efficiency. New fuel $\div$ old fuel $=\frac{24}{30}=0.8$: a 20 percent decrease. The 25 percent rise in efficiency does not cut fuel by 25 percent. Quantity B is greater.

content.quantityA: The percent decrease in the amount of fuel the driver uses each month
content.common: A driver replaces a car that averages 24 miles per gallon with a car that averages 30 miles per gallon and drives the same distance each month.

stem: A pump moves water at a constant rate of 0.6 cubic meter per minute. Given that 1 liter = 1,000 cubic centimeters, which of the following rates are equal to this rate? Indicate all such rates.
explanation: Convert the volume and the time separately. $0.6\cdot60=36$ cubic meters per hour. $0.6\text{ m}^3=0.6\cdot100^3\text{ cm}^3=600{,}000\text{ cm}^3$ per minute, which is 600 liters per minute, or $\frac{600}{60}=10$ liters per second. Correct: B, C and E.

choiceExplanations.A: Divides by 60 instead of multiplying: an hour has 60 minutes, so the hourly amount is 60 times larger.
choiceExplanations.D: Uses $100^2$ instead of $100^3$: cubic units need the length factor cubed.

stem: A flight leaves city F at 1:15 p.m. local time and lands in city G at 6:45 p.m. local time on the same day. The return flight leaves city G at 8:00 a.m. local time and lands in city F at 9:30 a.m. local time on the same day. Local time in city G is ahead of local time in city F, and the two flights take the same amount of time. How many hours does each flight take?
explanation: Let each flight take $T$ hours and let G be $z$ hours ahead of F. The first flight shows a clock difference of $5.5=T+z$; the return shows $1.5=T-z$. $T$ is the average of the two differences: $\frac{5.5+1.5}{2}=3.5$ (and $z=2$).

stem: A rectangular tank is 6 feet long, 4 feet wide, and 2.5 feet deep, and it contains water to a depth of 9 inches. Water is pumped in at 15 gallons per minute while a drain removes 3 gallons per minute. Given that 1 foot = 12 inches and 1 cubic foot = 7.5 gallons, how many minutes will it take to fill the tank?
explanation: Work in feet: 9 inches $=0.75$ foot, so the empty part is $6\cdot4\cdot(2.5-0.75)=42$ cubic feet, or $42\cdot7.5=315$ gallons. Net rate $=15-3=12$ gallons per minute. Time $=\frac{315}{12}=26.25$ minutes.
